description: The sea ice edge is the boundary between open water and ice-covered ocean, typically defined as a specific ice concentration threshold (commonly 15% concentration). The ice edge location is a key parameter for navigation, climate monitoring, and ecosystem studies, as it marks the transition zone between vastly different physical and biological regimes. For the Southern Ocean, the ice edge exhibits strong seasonal variability, with the Antarctic sea ice extent undergoing an annual cycle that sees the ice edge advance northward by hundreds of kilometers in winter and retreat close to the continent in summer. The marginal ice zone (MIZ) near the ice edge is characterized by complex ice-ocean-atmosphere interactions, enhanced biological productivity, and important marine mammal and seabird habitats. Ice edge position is derived from satellite observations including passive microwave, SAR, and optical imagery.
title: Sea Ice Edge
